blocks.text:
Drive into the Central Andes to reach Quilotoa, a crater lake formed by a major volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. The lake is about 250 m deep on average and is known for its bright turquoise water.

The hike follows the upper rim of the crater and takes about 4–5 hours. The lake stays in view from different points along the caldera rim, and the colour of the water shifts with the light. Afterwards, continue south into Chimborazo Province. On arrival, you’ll have time to relax.

**Accommodation:** Chimborazo Lodge.  
**Meals:** Breakfast, packed lunch and dinner.

blocks.text: Chimborazo and the Papallacta Hot Springs

provenance.rationale: The Word heading names the Chimborazo trek. The following itinerary names Papallacta Hot Springs as the second stop for this heading.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, set out on a trek around the base of Chimborazo. The trail crosses high-altitude wetlands where you may see alpacas and vicuñas and leads to a mountain refuge at around 5,000 m.

After the trek, drive to Papallacta, about four hours away. Your guide may change the route if the weather, trail conditions or how participants are feeling makes it unsafe.

Papallacta sits at about 3,220 m on one of the routes from the highlands to the Ecuadorian Amazon. It has a cool, humid climate, with average temperatures of around 10–14°C depending on the season. In 1542, Francisco de Orellana crossed the Andes along the route known as the Cinnamon Trail. His expedition went on to reach the Amazon River.

Spend the rest of the day at Termas de Papallacta, beside the Papallacta River. The complex has nine hot pools and three cold pools. The springs range from about 30 to 70°C and the pools from about 36 to 40°C. The water contains sulfates, sodium, calcium and magnesium chloride. The resort describes the water as having anti-inflammatory, soothing, antiallergic and diuretic properties.

**Accommodation:** Termas de Papallacta.  
**Meals:** Breakfast and packed lunch.
